name: MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline
title: MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline (MongoDB 8.0)

type.text: **Pipeline expressions are untyped**: A field path resolves to a BSON value of any type, and an operator applies to whatever the document carries
**Operators dispatch on the operand's run-time type**: `$add` on numbers, strings, and dates runs three different code paths chosen from the value
**No sum types**: An alternative is modelled with a discriminator field the expressions test by convention
**No generics**: A stage cannot be parameterised over a type, so reusable logic is copied, stored as a view, or wrapped in a JavaScript function
**Missing and NULL are distinct values**: A field can be absent, present as `NULL`, or present as a value, and comparisons over the three form a three-valued logic
**Expression names do not state their effects**: A pipeline shows the operators it runs, not the JavaScript effects an embedded function performs
**Embedded JavaScript crosses into the host runtime unchecked**: `$function` runs a JS body inside the server, and nothing checks it against the pipeline's expectations
**Pipeline variables are query-local**: `$let` and `$$ROOT` bind inside the pipeline, so no name is shared with another query

construction.text: **Stages build new documents**: Each stage produces its output documents, so the pipeline does not mutate its input in place
**Sub-pipelines compose without shared state**: `$lookup`, `$graphLookup`, and `$facet` build intermediate results inside the query
**Views store pipelines server-side**: A stored view is a dependency a reviewer must fetch from the deployment to read a query in full

memory.text: **The engine owns allocation**: Cursors, spool files, and intermediate results are managed by the server, not by the pipeline
**Unbounded stages can exhaust engine memory**: A `$group` over a large collection, a `$sort` with no `allowDiskUse`, or a dense `$lookup` can still fail the operation

error.text: **The pipeline has no construct that carries a failure**: A failing operator aborts the whole aggregation, and no language construct routes that failure to a handler
**A failure cannot travel as a value**: An expression has no result type that carries success-and-failure, so guarded evaluation is rebuilt with `$cond` and `$type` at every stage
**A failed aggregation writes nothing**: `$out` and `$merge` commit only when the pipeline completes, so an aborted pipeline leaves the target collection unchanged

concurrency.text: **The pipeline runs inside the engine's concurrency control**: The server schedules the operation, and its writes follow the storage engine's rules
**The language has no construct for concurrent work**: Parallelism is the engine's planner decision, not a pipeline author's choice

platform.text: **API-compatible servers exist**: Cosmos DB's Mongo API, FerretDB, and community ports run a growing share of the pipeline language
**Feature parity is chased, not promised**: A pipeline written to the latest server assumes stages, operators, and semantics that compatible servers reach at their own pace
**The pipeline is a poor fit outside document processing**: Multi-pass algorithms, external calls, and general application logic are pushed to the driver language or embedded JavaScript

performance.text: **The server compiles the pipeline to a plan**: The optimizer selects indexes and pipeline rewrites before execution
**Plan quality depends on the schema and the indexes**: The same pipeline is fast on a well-indexed collection and a table scan on a bare one

ecosystem.text: **Tooling fragments across compatible servers**: Drivers, consoles, and migration tools target MongoDB, Atlas, Cosmos DB, and FerretDB each with their own support level
**The engine, the tooling, and the documentation come from one vendor under licence**: Server licences have moved from Apache-2.0 to SSPL, and Atlas is a commercial service
**The ecosystem centres on one vendor's stack**: MongoDB Inc. ships the server, Atlas, Compass, and the official drivers, so its stack defines the idiomatic toolchain
**Two pipeline generations coexist**: v1 and v2 semantics and legacy stage forms must stay supported, so every new feature inherits the compatibility surface
**Official drivers cover the mainstream languages**: MongoDB maintains drivers for many ecosystems, and they are installed through ordinary package managers

evolution.text: **Server releases change pipeline semantics**: Operator behaviour, stage availability, and deprecated forms shift across major releases, so a pipeline is written against a version
**Release notes document each stage's availability**: Every stage and operator names the server version that introduced it
**Feature availability is gated by deployment configuration**: `featureCompatibilityVersion` and cluster topology decide which pipeline features a deployment runs

domain.text: **Adopting the pipeline means adopting a document store**: Stages, field paths, and update operators assume the document data model and the collections that hold it
**The pipeline is used to query stored document data and write results back**: `$match` retrieves documents, and `$merge` writes computed output into a collection
**Relational joins over nested arrays are verbose**: `$unwind` and `$lookup` chains replace the set logic many practitioners already know from SQL

learning.text: **Stage semantics are new material**: Field-path syntax, variable scope in `$lookup` and `$facet`, and missing-versus-NULL behaviour build on nothing a SQL practitioner carries
**The pipeline mixes three forms at once**: Dataflow stages, an expression language, and embedded JavaScript each offer their own way to write the same computation
**The manual documents every stage**: Per-stage reference pages with examples cover the common pipeline patterns

syntax.text: **Pipelines are verbose JSON**: Every stage is a wrapper object, every field path is a quoted string, and a small computation spans many nested braces
**Three quoting conventions share one tree**: Field paths are `$`-prefixed strings, operators are quoted names, and documents are JSON objects, so the mapping is not predictable
**The notation leans on the `$` sigil**: `"$field"`, `"$$var"`, and `"$add"` all put the same character in string position, so reading tracks the sigil to tell paths from operators
**A pipeline is data**: The stage array is a JSON document, so it round-trips through ordinary JSON tooling

testing.text: **No test harness ships with the language**: Testing a pipeline requires a running deployment and a harness each project builds for itself
**Type faults surface only on the documents reached**: An operator applied to the wrong BSON type fails when the aggregation processes a matching document, so an untested stage path gives no evidence
**No monotonic clock is published in the language**: `$$NOW` and `$$CLUSTER_TIME` read the wall clock, so elapsed-time behaviour depends on the deployment's clocks
**`explain()` reports the chosen plan**: Stage-by-stage plan output is standard practice for reviewing a pipeline

security.text: **Untrusted documents enter the pipeline untyped**: A stored document's field types are data, so an expression must re-check each type to survive hostile input
**A pipeline can embed executable code**: `$function` takes a JavaScript body that runs in the server, so a code string assembled from input is an injection path
**The pipeline is submitted as data, not as concatenated text**: A stage array built with a driver builder keeps values out of band, so a value cannot become syntax the way string-built SQL does

reproducibility.text: **A pipeline is data submitted as a request**: The same pipeline against the same server version and dataset reads the same result, and there is no build artifact to reproduce
**Pipelines live beside the application that submits them**: A deployment stores no manifest naming the server version the pipeline was written against

supplychain.text: **Published drivers carry no signed provenance by default**: A consumer must trust the package they install
**Drivers publish in registries with an ownership model**: The npm `mongodb` scope and Maven coordinates name the publisher, so there is no flat namespace to hijack
**No vulnerability advisory feed joins published drivers to known vulnerabilities at the package-version level**: A consumer reads release notes to learn a driver is affected

observability.text: **No stable tracing and metrics standard is part of the language**: Observability comes from the server profiler, Atlas, and driver-specific integrations
**No structured logging is defined in the language**: Diagnostics are server log entries with their own format
**Failed operations are recorded by the server**: The log and diagnostic captures name the pipeline and the failing stage

feedback.text: **The edit-test loop is a request submission**: There is no compile step between editing a pipeline and running it
**Drivers and consoles parse the pipeline before submission**: The JSON shape is checked while the author works
**No source-level debugger ships with the language**: Debugging is done through plan output, the server profiler, and log inspection

interop.text: **Embedded JavaScript calls host-language code**: `$function` and `$accumulator` run JS inside the engine without leaving the process
**The pipeline runs only inside a MongoDB-compatible server**: There is no portable target outside that context

governance.text: **MongoDB Inc. governs the pipeline's direction**: Stages ship with server releases, and no independent body decides the language
**No published specification defines the aggregation language**: The manual describes the shipping server, and compatible ports reached parity by differential testing against it
**No conformance suite exists**: Compatible servers cannot run a shared test suite against the pipeline language
**The pipeline is JSON, so any JSON parser reads the whole program**: The structure is available to tooling without reverse engineering

tradeoffs: **Untyped expressions keep pipelines flexible**: A stage processes any document shape, and type agreements move into every expression that reads a field
**NULL and missing keep optional data natural**: The document model needs no placeholder, and three-valued comparisons become a cost every reader pays
**Embedded JavaScript extends the pipeline**: `$function` buys general computation at the cost of an unchecked, injectable boundary inside the server
**Vendor-gated features buy velocity**: Stages arrive with server releases; the portability cost across compatible servers is a deliberate trade
verdict: The pipeline's untyped dataflow carries real language-imposed coupling: expressions apply to values of any type, operators dispatch at run time, and a failure has no path to a handler — it aborts the operation. Missing and NULL split comparisons into three-valued logic, and embedded JavaScript opens an unchecked boundary that is also an injection path. Main strengths: a declarative stage model the engine compiles to a plan, pipelines carried as data so there is no string-concatenation surface, and a driver ecosystem installed through ordinary package managers. Main weaknesses: the MongoDB licence history and single-vendor governance, no specification and no conformance suite for the compatible ports, two pipeline generations in service, and the learning cost of stage semantics that build on no prior skill.

energy.text: Runs inside a document database server: energy and time are the engine's, not the pipeline's.

ai-readiness.text: Pipeline JSON is heavily documented with public examples: current models write common stage sequences reliably, though multi-stage scoping bugs survive review.

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: The database server receives the pipeline as a JSON request and evaluates it; no compiled unit crosses a boundary.
